transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

It is actually normal for many Beko washer-dryers to use a small amount of cold water during the drying cycle. They work by condensing moisture from your clothes using a heat exchanger; this process requires a trickle of cold water to cool the system and flush the condensed water away through the drain. However, if it feels like excessive water or you hear gurgling/struggling sounds, there may be a blockage in the drainage path. Please check two things: first, is the water actually draining out properly (not pooling in the drum), and does the pump sound steady? Second, with the machine switched off and unplugged, please check the pump filter at the bottom front for any fluff or debris that might be restricting flow.

Thank you. Water isn't pooling in the drum and the clothes come out dry, and there's no leak on the floor. The pump sounds like it only runs occasionally. Is that all normal then, or do I still need to check the filter?

Yes, that is all normal. Since the clothes are coming out dry and there is no pooling or leaking, the water you hear is just the machine condensing moisture from your laundry using a small trickle of cold water, which it then pumps away occasionally as needed. You do not need to check the filter unless you notice poor drying performance in future. As a quick tip for next time, ensure you don't overload the drum with wet clothes when running a dry cycle, as washer-dryers have a smaller capacity for drying than washing.

candidates: Normal condensation process (cold water used to cool the heat exchanger) (high)
Blocked pump filter or drain path causing backup/recirculation (medium)
Faulty water inlet valve leaking continuously (low)
